doc.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Battles of the bands and the Lunceford brass sound
summary: They recall battles with Gene Krupa and Andy Kirk, and Lunceford's confidence, flugelhorns and French trumpets.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: You know that competition thing and that battle of the bands and the jam sessions, and I don’t know if that happens nowadays. But that must have really inspired players.
And made you play better than you thought maybe you could.
Oh, yeah. You probably play better than you ever played when you ever run across a band. You remember that battle we had at Washington, D.C. against Gene Krupa?
Yeah, and then we had a battle with I think it was Andy Kirk one night at the Golden Gate Ballroom.

But the Lunceford band was so tough that we weren’t worried about any band. We just weren’t worried about any band because we didn’t even bother to take out our music when we played the battle of the bands because you only played, you know you played a set, and we wouldn’t even have any bandstand. We’d just come in and do our thing. If you would notice the Lunceford band, they had it right from the trumpets, they had trumpet, flugelhorn and the little French trumpets. They had, oh, they were a tough band.
A lot of people don’t know that, but Lunceford’s band was one of the first bands that had flugelhorns in the band, I would say.
Yeah. And the little French trumpet, it’s made like a French horn, but it’s a B flat trumpet.
